correctness.rationale: The consecutive-layer convex hull is proved directly to equal the cube intersected with the two sum halfspaces: any vertex of that intersection is 0/1. Ball containment is therefore exactly the system c_i>=r, c_i<=1-r, sum(c)>=a+r sqrt(d), sum(c)<=b-r sqrt(d). Feasibility reduces to intersection of the two scalar sum intervals [dr,d(1-r)] and [a+r sqrt(d),b-r sqrt(d)], whose four cross-endpoint inequalities give precisely the four terms in the claimed minimum. The full optimal-center set is the same system at r=r_*. Equality cases prove the uniqueness criterion; when the slab-width term is strictly dominant, the center set is an interior hyperplane slice of the box and has dimension d-1.

value.rationale: S-hypersimplices are a named family introduced to unify cubes, classical hypersimplices, cross-polytopes, and halfcubes, and the consecutive-layer subfamily already supports independent work on its graph metric. The theorem gives a complete ambient Euclidean Chebyshev classification for every consecutive interval of layers: exact radius, all centers, uniqueness, and a four-mechanism phase diagram. The appearance of a positive-dimensional optimal-center family exactly in the strict slab-width phase is structural information not visible from the existing face or graph-distance theory.
